transcript.text: What's she wearing?

setting: Dilbert's desk at his office computer
situation: Dilbert proudly explains that his new anti-spam software scans incoming e-mail for keywords and deletes anything that looks like an advertisement. Dogbert poses a hypothetical: a beautiful Victoria's Secret model e-mails him an invitation to date on her sailboat, but misspells 'sail' as 'sale'. After a silent beat, Dilbert's only response is to ask what she's wearing.
punchline: Dilbert's lonely, lustful curiosity instantly overrides his belief in his spam filter's logic, showing he would gladly read a probable advertisement if a beautiful woman seemed to be offering a date.
summary: A programmer's confident explanation of his email filter collapses when his dog's hypothetical about an alluring message makes him care far more about the sender than the software.

file: 2000/2000-07-03_boss_crazy_fear_introcutions_jumpy_lulu_no sense of proportion_over reacts_scared.gif
title: Lulu Overreacts to Everything

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Dilbert, you'll be working with Lulu. She's almost normal.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: But she has no sense of proportion for problems.

transcript.speaker: Lulu
transcript.text: Did you notice that he looked at you funny?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: What?!

situation: The Boss introduces Dilbert to his new coworker Lulu, calling her almost normal, and warns that she has no sense of proportion about problems. Dilbert shakes her hand, and Lulu immediately points out that the Boss looked at him funny, alarming Dilbert over a trivial non-event.
punchline: The Boss's warning is proven instantly true when Lulu treats a funny look as a serious problem, rattling Dilbert and revealing she is far from normal.
summary: A new coworker's inability to judge how serious a problem is gets demonstrated within seconds of meeting her.

file: 2000/2000-01-04_dogcart consults_data minig_another message_stealing lunches_refigerator_break room_pudding.gif
title: Data Mining Finds Message From God

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Dogbert consults

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: My data-mining software has found another message from God.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: It says you've been stealing lunches from the refrigerator in the break room.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Then it says, "Ha ha, that wasn't pudding!"

setting: Office, across a desk during a consulting session
situation: Dogbert, acting as a consultant, tells the Boss that his data-mining software has found another message from God. The message accuses the Boss of stealing lunches from the break room refrigerator, then adds a taunting punchline that the food he ate was not pudding. The Boss sits uncomfortably, then rests his chin on his hand in resignation.
punchline: Dogbert uses fake 'divine' data-mining output as a pretext to deliver a prank, revealing the Boss ate something gross that he mistook for pudding.
summary: A consulting dog claims his software decodes divine messages and uses it to accuse his client of lunch theft and a nasty surprise.

file: 2000/2000-06-26_plan_agreement_happy_cheers_inspiring.gif
title: Boss Mistakes Pager Cheers For Inspiration

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: ...And that's the plan.

transcript.speaker: Ted
transcript.text: Yippee!

transcript.speaker: Carol
transcript.text: Woo-ha!!

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I'm very inspiring lately.

transcript.speaker: Carol
transcript.text: How did people survive meetings before these things?

transcript.speaker: Ted
transcript.text: WebVan split!

situation: The Boss finishes presenting his plan and two employees at the table cheer enthusiastically. He thinks his inspiring leadership has won them over. In the last panel the two employees are seen holding handheld devices and the cheers were really a reaction to the stock news on them, not to him.
punchline: The employees were cheering over a stock split announcement on their handheld devices, not the Boss's plan, so his belief that he is inspiring is totally mistaken.
summary: A manager basks in what he assumes is applause for his speech, while his audience was actually celebrating stock news on their gadgets.

file: 2000/2000-06-02_every person_on earth_one person_the entire world_tibetan monks_ugly website.gif
title: Everyone Says Website Is Ugly

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Ming, everyone says our web site is ugly.

transcript.speaker: Ming
transcript.text: Really? Every person on Earth said that?

transcript.speaker: Ming
transcript.text: Even Tibetan monks?

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Maybe it was just one person.

transcript.speaker: Ming
transcript.text: And you confused him with the entire planet?

situation: The Boss tells Ming, the web designer, that everyone says the company web site is ugly. Ming sarcastically questions whether literally every person on Earth, even Tibetan monks, said so. The Boss backpedals that it may have been just one person, and Ming points out he mistook one critic for the whole planet.
punchline: The Boss's sweeping claim of universal criticism collapses under mild scrutiny, revealing he is generalizing from a single complaint.
summary: A manager relays sweeping criticism of the company site, and the designer gleefully deflates the exaggeration.

file: 2000/2000-05-01_career_important assignment_folder_office equipment_problems at home.gif
title: Asset Tags Prompt Asok's Tantrum

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Asok, this will be the most important assignment in your entire career.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: You must affix the asset tags in this folder to our office equipment.

transcript.speaker: Asok
transcript.text: Bwaa-wah-ah!!

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: He must be having problems at home.

situation: The Boss solemnly tells Asok that his next task is the most important assignment of his entire career. The task turns out to be sticking asset tags on office equipment, and Asok breaks down sobbing. The Boss, oblivious, assumes Asok's outburst comes from trouble at home.
punchline: The Boss hypes a menial sticker-labeling chore as a career-defining job and then blames Asok's personal life for his despair instead of recognizing the work is demeaning.
summary: A manager inflates a trivial labeling chore into a pinnacle of achievement, then misreads his young employee's crying as a domestic issue.

file: 2000/2000-03-01_where he hid files_disgruntled_porcelain patty_job resigned.gif
title: Searching Restroom Stalls for Missing Files

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Ted resigned. Your job is to find out where he hid his files.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Our only clue is that he was disgruntled.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Negatory on porcelain patty.

setting: The Boss's office, then a restroom
situation: The Boss tells an employee that Ted has resigned and that he must locate the files Ted hid. The only clue is that Ted was disgruntled, so the employee ends up checking a restroom with a clipboard, apparently reasoning that a disgruntled person would hide files in the toilet.
punchline: The Boss's 'disgruntled' clue is so vague that the employee resorts to searching a restroom, using a pun on 'disgruntled' as the hint for the hiding place and reporting on it in goofy radio-style jargon.
summary: A manager sends a worker off to hunt for a departed colleague's hidden data with nothing but a pun-worthy clue, and the search ends in the bathroom.

file: 2000/2000-02-23_demo of new prodcut_ceo_partner is channeling_angry energy_thousand dead souls_more like that.gif
title: Channeling the Angry Energy of Dead Souls

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Put together a demo of our new product. Our CEO wants to see it.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: My partner is channeling the angry energy of a thousand dead souls.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Why can't you be more like that?

situation: The Boss orders Dilbert and his coworker to prepare a demo of the new product for the CEO. Dilbert explains that his partner is busy channeling the angry energy of a thousand dead souls. Rather than being alarmed, The Boss asks why Dilbert can't be more like that.
punchline: The Boss treats a coworker's disturbing, supernatural rage as an admirable work ethic, showing how management values intensity over sanity or actual results.
summary: A manager responds to a coworker's spooky, seething fury with envy, wishing his other employee would act the same way.

file: 2000/2000-08-14_not nine_start at 8am_ten minutes early_work start_late_tardy_hour late.gif
title: Early Arrival Costs Wally Ten Minutes

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: I was so motivated by your pep talk yesterday that I came to work ten minutes early!

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Wally, we start at eight, not at nine.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: That's gonna cost you ten minutes.

situation: Wally stands before the Boss's desk and proudly announces that he arrived ten minutes early because of the Boss's pep talk. The Boss points out that work starts at eight, not nine, which means Wally was actually an hour late. The Boss then says the lateness will cost Wally ten minutes, apparently of his pay or time.
punchline: Wally's supposed early arrival was really a late one, and the Boss turns his boasting into a penalty, showing that a slacker's effort gets punished while the misunderstanding gets him nowhere.
summary: A lazy employee brags about arriving early, only to learn he showed up an hour after the real start time and gets docked for it.

file: 2000/2000-06-17_meeting_strange words_make sense_pow_buy card_business.gif
title: Understanding the Meeting Is Fatal

transcript.speaker: Coworker
transcript.text: Uh-oh... suddenly this meeting and all the strange words make sense.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: POW!!

transcript.speaker: Bald Coworker
transcript.text: It's your turn to buy the card.

situation: Three men sit at a conference table. The man in the middle realizes with alarm that the meeting and its jargon suddenly make sense to him, and he explodes in a burst of smoke. The bald coworker calmly remarks that it is someone else's turn to buy the card, as if this happens regularly.
punchline: Actually comprehending corporate meeting jargon is lethal, and the colleagues treat the resulting death as routine enough to just rotate who buys the sympathy card.
summary: A man who finally grasps the meeting's baffling buzzwords blows up on the spot, and his colleague casually notes whose turn it is to buy the condolence card.

file: 2000/2000-01-21_charge fee_investments_removing tonsils_years of training.gif
title: Billing for Doing Nothing

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Dogbert Investments

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: So, you charge a fee every year even if you do nothing?

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: It takes years of training to know when to do nothing.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: I guess that makes sense.

transcript.speaker: Client
transcript.text: Here's my bill for not removing your tonsils.

situation: A client questions Dogbert, an investment advisor, about charging an annual fee even when he does nothing with the client's money. Dogbert claims it takes years of training to know when to do nothing. The client accepts this logic and hands Dogbert a bill for not removing his tonsils.
punchline: The client turns Dogbert's own justification against him by billing him for the absurd non-service of not performing surgery, exposing how ridiculous charging for inaction is.
summary: An investment client accepts his advisor's excuse for charging fees to do nothing, then sends back an equally ridiculous invoice for surgery he never performed.

file: 2000/2000-07-25_didn't ask_erased hard drive_mansplain_reformatting hard drive_step aside_upgardes.gif
title: IT Upgrade Wipes Another Hard Drive

transcript.speaker: IS Technician
transcript.text: Step aside. I'm from I.S.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: I didn't ask for any upgrades.

transcript.speaker: IS Technician
transcript.text: That's what they all say until...

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: It's reformatting my hard drive!

transcript.speaker: IS Technician
transcript.text: That's ten in a row. Maybe it's me.

situation: An I.S. technician walks up to Alice's cubicle with a screwdriver and a manual, tells her to step aside, and starts working on her computer even though she never requested any upgrades. Moments later her hard drive is being reformatted, and the technician casually admits it has now happened ten times in a row.
punchline: The technician only half-jokingly suspects that he himself is the cause of the repeated data-wiping disasters, yet shows no real concern or accountability.
summary: An overconfident tech support worker barges into a cubicle uninvited and ends up erasing yet another employee's computer.

file: 2000/2000-03-08_cancel others_crazy ideas_one you of ten_research projects_research and development.gif
title: Cancel the Nine Failing Projects

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: One out of ten research and development projects will succeed.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: I recommend cancelling the other nine.

transcript.speaker: Tina
transcript.text: I wonder where he gets all these crazy ideas.

setting: Conference room during a meeting, then a lunch table
situation: Wally tells the boss that only one in ten R&D projects will succeed and recommends cancelling the other nine. The boss listens from his chair. Later, Wally eats lunch with Tina and Dilbert while Tina wonders aloud where he gets his crazy ideas.
punchline: Wally's 'recommendation' is absurd because nobody can know in advance which one project will succeed, so cancelling the other nine is nonsense, yet colleagues treat it as a quirky idea rather than flawed logic.
summary: A coworker confidently proposes culling most of the company's research efforts based on a simple success statistic, leaving his lunch companions baffled by his thinking.

file: 2000/2000-08-13_can't breathe_demonstration_evil eye process_new consultant_paper cut bleeding_rasputin_charisma.gif
title: Rasputin's Charisma Demonstration Backfires

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: This is Rasputin, our new consultant.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: He stopped my paper cut from bleeding.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: He has charisma.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: I'd like to see a demonstration on Asok.

transcript.speaker: Asok
transcript.text: Ack... Can't... Breathe...

transcript.speaker: Rasputin
transcript.text: That's called the evil eye process.

transcript.speaker: Rasputin
transcript.text: Now do Wally.

transcript.speaker: Rasputin
transcript.text: Ack... Can't... Breathe...

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: He never had a chance.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Your anti-charisma is strong today.

situation: The Boss introduces Rasputin, a mystical consultant, and praises his charisma by claiming he stopped a paper cut from bleeding. Alice asks for a demonstration on Asok, who gasps for air under the evil eye. Rasputin then tries the same on Wally, but Rasputin ends up choking and collapsing while Wally is unaffected.
punchline: Wally's legendary lack of charisma is so powerful that it overwhelms even the evil eye of a supposed mystic, leaving the consultant helpless.
summary: A mystical consultant's hypnotic powers work on a coworker but crumble when he targets the one employee who is immune to all influence.

file: 2000/2000-02-18_arm hair growth_on phone_wait in hall_hair growing nicely_wait for boss_phone call_asked to wait.gif
title: Waiting For The Boss's Call

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: He's on the phone. You'll have to stand here and wait.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Don't leave. Don't make noise. Don't try talking to me.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Arm hair LX-943 is growing nicely.

situation: Dilbert is told by a coworker (the boss's gatekeeper) that the boss is on the phone and he must stand and wait without leaving, making noise, or talking to her. With nothing else to do, Dilbert stands in front of the boss's desk and passes the time by checking his own arm hair, which he has numbered like a lab specimen.
punchline: Forced to wait idly with no permitted activity, Dilbert is reduced to monitoring the growth of his arm hair, showing how boring and pointless the waiting is.
summary: Barred from doing anything while he waits for his boss to finish a call, Dilbert entertains himself by observing the progress of his arm hair.

file: 2000/2000-08-09_poach employees_leave comapny_wink wink_moron.gif
title: Wink Wink Job Poaching Loophole

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I'm not allowed to poach employees if I leave this company.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: But there's no law against you asking me for a job...wink wink.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I'm not going to wink all day, you moron!

situation: The Boss tells Dilbert that he can't poach employees if he leaves the company, but hints that Dilbert is free to ask him for a job. He winks conspicuously to signal what he wants. When Dilbert fails to pick up on the hint, the Boss angrily scolds him for being too dense.
punchline: The Boss's attempt at a subtle legal loophole is so obvious and clumsy that he gets angry at Dilbert for not responding quickly enough to his exaggerated winking.
summary: A boss planning to leave awkwardly hints that his subordinate should ask him for a job, then loses patience when the hint isn't taken.

file: 2000/2000-07-09_dna_feed her_human genome_human simulations_invented_mapped and decoded_market application_on computer watch_punish her_samples_software_software simulation_engineering.gif
title: Simulated Woman Who Refuses Dates

transcript.speaker: Engineer
transcript.text: My software will create human simulations from DNA samples.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: What's the market application?

transcript.speaker: Engineer
transcript.text: Well... there are many various applications.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Name one.

transcript.speaker: Engineer
transcript.text: Well... someday the entire human genome will be mapped and decoded.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: You could take a hair sample from a woman who refuses to date you...

transcript.speaker: Engineer
transcript.text: And create a software simulation of her to keep in your computer watch.

transcript.speaker: Engineer
transcript.text: You could have one button to feed her and one button to punish her.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: I'd buy it.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Can you add a button?

setting: Conference room during a product presentation
situation: An engineer presents software that creates human simulations from DNA samples, but when pressed by Dilbert for a market application he can only offer vague talk about the human genome. He then pitches a creepy use: simulating a woman who refuses to date you, with buttons to feed and punish her. Wally and the Boss are eager buyers, and the Boss asks for another button.
punchline: The only market the engineer can find for his technology is a creepy stalker gadget for punishing women who reject you, and the Boss's only concern is adding more buttons.
summary: A researcher struggling to justify his DNA-based simulation software lands on a disturbing pitch that his colleagues enthusiastically embrace.

file: 2000/2000-03-02_files_hid files_skeleton_babe_home wrecker.gif
title: Asok Adopts Skeleton as Desk Companion

transcript.speaker: Asok
transcript.text: I have found where Ted hid his files before he quit.

transcript.speaker: Asok
transcript.text: A skeleton!

transcript.speaker: Asok
transcript.text: I know what I must do.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: Who's the babe?

transcript.speaker: Asok
transcript.text: Stay away, homewrecker.

setting: Office storage room and Asok's cubicle
situation: Asok discovers the files Ted hid before quitting, along with a skeleton in the storage closet. He brings the skeleton back to his cubicle, dresses it with a wig, and sits it beside him at his desk. Wally, holding a coffee mug, asks who the babe is, and Asok jealously warns him off.
punchline: Asok is so lonely and desperate for companionship that he treats a skeleton in a wig as his girlfriend and accuses Wally of trying to steal her.
summary: A lonely young employee dresses up a skeleton he found in a closet and guards it as if it were his date.

file: 2000/2000-06-29_any errand_date women_film_movies_ratbert_thinks wally is hot_entertainment.gif
title: Ratbert Provides a Date Who Flatters

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Ratbert the Concierge

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: I'd like a date with a woman who thinks I'm hot.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: Remember, you promised you would do any errand for employees.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: Tell me again how hot I am.

setting: Concierge desk in the office, then a movie theater
situation: Ratbert is working as the office concierge, and Wally asks him to arrange a date with a woman who thinks Wally is hot, reminding Ratbert that he promised to run any errand for employees. In the last panel Wally sits in a movie theater beside Ratbert, who is wearing a wig, and asks to be told again how hot he is.
punchline: Ratbert fulfils the request by disguising himself as Wally's date, so Wally ends up fishing for compliments from a rat in a wig.
summary: A lazy coworker leans on a concierge's pledge to run any errand and ends up on a cinema date that is not quite what he pictured.

file: 2000/2000-05-30_no click shopping_patent_whiners_ship books.gif
title: No-Click Shopping Patent Threat

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: My patent for no-click shopping was granted.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I'm sure some whiners will say it's an obvious idea.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: You'd better click something or I have to ship you some books.

situation: Dogbert walks up to Dilbert, who is working at his computer, and announces that his patent for no-click shopping has been granted. He preempts criticism that the idea is obvious. He then threatens Dilbert that unless he clicks something, Dogbert will ship him books anyway.
punchline: A no-click shopping system means purchases happen automatically without the customer's consent, so Dogbert can force unwanted products on Dilbert unless he actively intervenes, mocking both obvious patents and aggressive e-commerce.
summary: Dogbert boasts about a freshly granted patent for buying things without clicking, then menaces Dilbert with unrequested book deliveries.

file: 2000/2000-04-13_technology buddha_enlightened_eat a lot_tell people ideas_shoe scrape.gif
title: Technology Buddha Scrapes Ideas Off Shoe

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Technology Buddha

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: How did you become so enlightened?

transcript.speaker: Technology Buddha
transcript.text: I just eat a lot and tell people their ideas stink.

transcript.speaker: Technology Buddha
transcript.text: Whose shoe did you scrape this off of?

setting: Office of the Technology Buddha, a desk and large chair
situation: Dilbert approaches a smug, serene-looking guru called the Technology Buddha and asks how he became so enlightened. The Buddha reveals his method is simply eating a lot and criticizing other people's ideas. When Dilbert hands over a paper with an idea, the Buddha rejects it by insulting it as something scraped off a shoe.
punchline: The supposed technology guru's wisdom is nothing more than eating and dismissing everyone else's ideas as garbage, which he then demonstrates by trashing Dilbert's proposal.
summary: A self-styled tech sage admits his guru status rests on overeating and trashing other people's proposals, then promptly insults the idea Dilbert brings him.

file: 2000/2000-03-31_dumpster service_save money_discovered alternative costs_tear off piece.gif
title: Dumpster Service Replaced By Pockets

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I cancelled our dumpster service to save money.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I discovered an alternative that costs nothing.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Everyone tear off a piece and put it in your pocket.

situation: The Boss tells his team at a conference table that he cancelled the company's dumpster service to cut costs. His free alternative is to have every employee tear off a piece of the trash on the table and carry it away in their pockets.
punchline: The boss's cost-saving scheme simply shifts the burden of garbage disposal onto employees, who must literally carry the company's trash home in their pockets.
summary: A manager axes the garbage contract and cheerfully instructs his staff to pocket the rubbish themselves.

file: 2000/2000-06-22_radio_sing_don't like to talk_hum_pretend radio_no talking dates.gif
title: Date Hums, Dilbert Wants Radio

transcript.speaker: Dilbert's Date
transcript.text: I don't like to talk on dates. Do you mind if I hum?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: That's okay. I'll pretend you're the radio.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert's Date
transcript.text: Hmm mm-m mm-m-m m mm mm

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I need a new radio.

setting: Inside Dilbert's red car, driving on a date
situation: Dilbert is driving his date somewhere when she announces she dislikes talking on dates and asks if she can hum instead. Dilbert politely agrees and says he'll pretend she is the radio. Once she starts humming tunelessly, he privately thinks that he needs a new radio.
punchline: Dilbert's attempt to be accommodating backfires because his date's humming is so bad that it makes him wish for an actual radio instead.
summary: A woman who hates chatting on dates offers to hum, and her driver soon regrets treating her as his car stereo.

file: 2000/2000-01-16_have none_intern_know how_semi colons_skills_teaching_tech suport_useful skills_cubicle_education.gif
title: Tina Exploits Asok's Technical Skills

transcript.speaker: Tina
transcript.text: Asok, can you help me install an Ethernet card?

transcript.speaker: Asok
transcript.text: Tina, I am not your personal tech support.

transcript.speaker: Tina
transcript.text: But you know how to do it and I don't.

transcript.speaker: Asok
transcript.text: Well...that is true.

transcript.speaker: Tina
transcript.text: Could you carry the PC to my new cubicle? It's too heavy for me.

transcript.speaker: Asok
transcript.text: Someday I'll repay you by teaching you about semi-colons.

transcript.speaker: Asok
transcript.text: How come I have many useful skills and you have none?

transcript.speaker: Tina
transcript.text: I guess I'm just lucky.

situation: Tina asks Asok to install an Ethernet card in her PC. Asok objects that he isn't her personal tech support, but agrees when she points out he knows how and she doesn't. She then gets him to carry her heavy PC to her new cubicle, and he wonders aloud why he has many skills and she has none.
punchline: Tina's lack of skills is actually her greatest skill, since she keeps getting capable people like Asok to do her work for her, which she cheerfully acknowledges as luck.
summary: A helpless coworker talks a skilled colleague into doing her technical chores and heavy lifting, leaving him puzzled by the unfairness of it all.
keywords: getting others to do your work

file: 2000/2000-08-04_purse stolen_navy seal training_booby trap cubcile_early mail delivery_hurt mailman_catch a thief.gif
title: Booby-Trapped Cubicle Catches Mailman

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Someone stole my purse.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: So I used my Navy SEAL training to booby-trap my cubicle.

transcript.speaker: Off-panel voice
transcript.text: AAIEE!!!

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: The mail is early today.

setting: Office, Alice's cubicle and the boss's office
situation: Alice tells her boss that someone stole her purse. She explains that she used her Navy SEAL training to booby-trap her cubicle. A scream is heard off-panel, and Alice calmly checks her watch and remarks that the mail is early today, implying the mail carrier triggered her trap.
punchline: Alice's lethal booby trap has just injured an innocent mail carrier, and she responds with detached indifference, noting only that he arrived early.
summary: After a theft, a fiercely trained employee rigs her workspace with traps, and the first victim is a hapless mail deliverer whose injury she treats as a scheduling quirk.

file: 2000/2000-01-14_early business trip_won by default_secretary uses office.gif
title: Boss Wins By Default, Secretary Surprise

transcript.speaker: Coworker
transcript.text: Look who's back early from his business trip.

transcript.speaker: Coworker
transcript.text: How did it go?

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Excellent! I won every meeting by default. The other side never showed up.

transcript.speaker: Coworker
transcript.text: Did you know your secretary uses your office when you're gone?

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: For what?

setting: Office hallway and the Boss's office
situation: A coworker holding a coffee mug greets the Boss, who has returned early from a business trip. The Boss proudly claims he won every meeting because the other side never showed up. The coworker then casually mentions that the Boss's secretary uses his office while he is away, and the Boss asks what for, while a man is visible on a desk in the office behind them.
punchline: The Boss is too oblivious to realize that his 'victory' was really a no-show and that his secretary is using his office for something improper, implied to be an affair.
summary: A manager brags about a hollow business trip triumph, then walks straight into a hint about what happens in his office when he's away.

file: 2000/2000-06-05_mordac_preventer_information services_web mistress_firewall inadequate_talk cobol baby.gif
title: Mordac Meets Web Mistress Ming

transcript.speaker: Mordac
transcript.text: I am Mordac, the Preventer of Information Services!

transcript.speaker: Web Mistress Ming
transcript.text: I am Web Mistress Ming!

transcript.speaker: Mordac
transcript.text: Your firewall is inadequate. You must be punished!

transcript.speaker: Web Mistress Ming
transcript.text: Your HTML is weak! You must be punished.

transcript.speaker: Mordac
transcript.text: I must have you!

transcript.speaker: Web Mistress Ming
transcript.text: Talk COBOL to me, baby.

situation: Mordac, the head of information services, introduces himself to Web Mistress Ming, who is seated at her computer. They trade technical insults about her firewall and his HTML, each declaring the other must be punished. The exchange turns into an embrace, with Mordac grabbing her and asking her to talk COBOL to him.
punchline: The two IT tyrants swap geeky threats like flirtation, and their mutual hostility turns into romance, with obsolete COBOL programming talk serving as dirty talk.
summary: Two domineering tech workers trade nerdy insults and promptly fall into a passionate embrace.

file: 2000/2000-07-07_employee of month_lulu_overcame odds_to win_name randomly picked_victory_last month.gif
title: Employee of the Month Randomly Chosen

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: The employee of the month is Lulu.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Lulu overcame long odds to win this award.

transcript.speaker: Man in yellow shirt
transcript.text: I.e., her name was randomly picked.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: I'd protest but I don't want to taint my victory of last month.

situation: The Boss announces that Lulu is the employee of the month, saying she overcame long odds. A coworker in a yellow shirt clarifies that this just means her name was picked at random. Wally says he won't protest, because he doesn't want to taint his own victory from the previous month.
punchline: Wally implies that he won the award last month through random chance too, and he's gladly keeping a meaningless honor intact rather than questioning its legitimacy.
summary: An office honor turns out to be a lottery draw, and a lazy coworker declines to object since his own past win was equally unearned.

file: 2000/2000-01-07_bonus is 5%_don't feel bad_salary_salary differences_the boss_intern ages_inequity_allow to feel bad_money.gif
title: Same Bonus Percentage, Unequal Salaries

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Asok, your bonus is only 5% this year. Don't feel bad; I only got 5% too.

transcript.speaker: Asok
transcript.text: But 5% of your salary is four times more than 5% of my salary.

transcript.speaker: Asok
transcript.text: May I feel bad about that?

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Sure. Go wild!

situation: The Boss tells Asok that his bonus is only 5% this year and tries to console him by saying he also got only 5%. Asok points out that 5% of the Boss's salary is four times larger than 5% of his own. He asks permission to feel bad about it, and the Boss cheerfully allows it.
punchline: The Boss's attempt at solidarity ignores the huge pay gap, and when Asok points it out, he shrugs it off by granting permission to feel bad, showing he doesn't care about the inequity.
summary: A manager claims shared misfortune over a small bonus until his intern shows the numbers aren't remotely comparable.

file: 2000/2000-06-07_emails_love emails_threats of firing_dating boss_regrets.gif
title: Love Letter With Recycling Threat

transcript.speaker: Mordac
transcript.text: Dearest Ming, my love for you is boundless. Mordac

transcript.speaker: Mordac
transcript.text: P.S. If you don't stop putting food garbage in the recycling bin you will be terminated.

transcript.speaker: Ming
transcript.text: Never date your boss.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Okay.

situation: Mordac types a love email to his employee Ming, professing boundless love, then tacks on a postscript threatening to fire her for putting food garbage in the recycling bin. Ming, reading it at her desk, offers a warning about dating your boss, and Dilbert agrees.
punchline: A romantic email from a boss turns into a firing threat over trivial recycling rules, showing why dating your boss is a terrible idea.
summary: A manager's affectionate message to a subordinate ends with a petty termination threat, prompting her cautionary advice about workplace romance.

file: 2000/2000-02-07_website_business case_web productivity commitee_technology.gif
title: Blocked Website Requires Business Case

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I need to see a web site that's blocked by our I.S. group.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Submit a business case to the Web Productivity and Security Committee.

transcript.speaker: Snail
transcript.text: Hey, bro, where's your shell? This ain't Casual Day.

setting: Office, the Boss's desk and Dilbert's cubicle
situation: Dilbert tells the Boss he needs access to a website that the I.S. group has blocked. The Boss tells him to submit a business case to the Web Productivity and Security Committee. Dilbert then goes to his computer, where a snail addresses him in slang and scolds him about his missing shell.
punchline: Going through the committee's bureaucratic approval process is so slow that a snail stands in for the committee, and the snail mocks Dilbert for lacking a shell on a day that isn't Casual Day.
summary: A request to unblock a website sends an employee into a slow committee process, personified by a wisecracking snail.

file: 2000/2000-04-06_fake disability leave_missed camaraderie_stimulating conversation_didn't know gone_not missed.gif
title: Nobody Noticed Wally Was Gone

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: I came back early from my fake disability leave.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: I missed the camaraderie and the stimulating conversation.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I didn't know you were gone.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: Not bad for a Tuesday.

situation: Wally, holding a coffee mug, tells Dilbert he returned early from a fake disability leave because he missed the camaraderie and stimulating conversation of work. Dilbert, busy at his computer, says he never realized Wally was gone. Wally responds that going unnoticed is a decent accomplishment for a Tuesday.
punchline: Wally is so lazy and invisible at work that his absence went completely unnoticed, and he treats that as a small victory rather than an insult.
summary: A slacker who faked a disability leave discovers his coworker never even noticed he was away, and he takes that as a win.

file: 2000/2000-03-21_from the future_time machine invention_stick finger_hole.gif
title: Future Dilbert Demands Finger in Hole

transcript.speaker: Sound effect
transcript.text: ZZOOP!

transcript.speaker: Future Dilbert
transcript.text: I am you from the future. Your time machine invention works.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: How does my head get like that?

transcript.speaker: Future Dilbert
transcript.text: Stick a finger in this hole.

situation: Dilbert sits at his computer when an older, heavier version of himself materializes in a flash and announces that Dilbert's time machine works. Dilbert only asks why the visitor's head looks so strange, and the future self responds by telling him to stick a finger in a hole in the device he is holding.
punchline: Instead of any useful knowledge about the future, the time traveler's only message is a suspicious, gag-setting instruction to stick a finger in a hole, implying a prank or trap.
summary: A time-traveling older Dilbert proves the invention works, then abruptly invites his younger self to poke a finger into a mysterious hole.
keywords: stick a finger in the hole

file: 2000/2000-03-12_stirrup pants_not professional_filed patent_50 million dollars_earn license fees_comapny_various pant crises.gif
title: Pants Policing Over Fifty-Million Patent

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Alice.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Stirrup pants are not professional attire.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: I just filed a patent that will earn fifty million in license fees for the company.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Really? Wow.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: But it's no excuse for bad pants.

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Whatever. Did you sign the budget request I gave you last week?

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: No...I've been busy with various pant-related crises.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Here's another.

situation: The Boss stops Alice to criticize her stirrup pants as unprofessional. Alice says she has just filed a patent worth fifty million dollars to the company, but he insists that is no excuse for bad pants. When she asks whether he signed her budget request, he says he has been too busy with pant-related crises, and he imagines yet another pair of pants.
punchline: The Boss is so fixated on trivial dress-code details that he ignores a huge accomplishment and neglects his actual job of approving budgets.
summary: A manager obsesses over an employee's fashion choices while brushing off her lucrative invention and leaving her paperwork unsigned.

file: 2000/2000-07-15_stress_use as excuse_not exercising_made me the man.gif
title: Stress as Excuse Not to Exercise

transcript.speaker: Coworker
transcript.text: I got the stress everyone talks about. What should I do?

transcript.speaker: Bald Coworker
transcript.text: Try using it as an excuse for not exercising.

transcript.speaker: Coworker
transcript.text: So... it's a good thing?

transcript.speaker: Bald Coworker
transcript.text: It made me the man I am today.

situation: A worried coworker tells a seated, bald, bespectacled colleague that he is suffering from workplace stress and asks for advice. The colleague suggests using the stress as a reason to skip exercise. When asked whether stress is therefore a good thing, the colleague claims it made him the man he is today, which is clearly out of shape.
punchline: The colleague's self-satisfied claim that stress shaped him is a dry joke at his own expense, since the result is a sedentary, unfit man who thinks avoiding exercise is a benefit.
summary: Asked how to cope with job stress, a sedentary coworker recommends it as a handy excuse to skip the gym and proudly credits it for his current state.
keywords: made me the man I am today

file: 2000/2000-07-23_baby cio_meeting_diapers_nature calls_big words_very advanced_baby_infany_genius_smart_talks_business.gif
title: The Baby CIO Needs Changing

transcript.speaker: Carol
transcript.text: Have you met the new CIO?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Carol
transcript.text: I hear he's young.

transcript.speaker: Baby CIO
transcript.text: Hello.

transcript.speaker: Baby CIO
transcript.text: We need to integrate our enterprise resource planning with our existing e-commerce platform.

transcript.speaker: Baby CIO
transcript.text: Now if you'll excuse me, nature calls.

transcript.speaker: Baby CIO
transcript.text: Aaahhh...

transcript.speaker: Baby CIO
transcript.text: Then we'll de-centralize the procurement function and...

transcript.speaker: Baby CIO
transcript.text: Hold on a second.

transcript.speaker: Baby CIO
transcript.text: Gramps, could you do me a huge favor?

situation: Carol tells Dilbert the new CIO is young, and a diaper-wearing toddler walks into the meeting and takes the CIO's seat. He speaks fluently in IT jargon about integrating ERP and e-commerce, then excuses himself because nature calls. After relieving himself in his diaper, he resumes the jargon and asks a coworker to change him.
punchline: The new CIO is literally a baby who speaks perfect business buzzwords but still needs his diaper changed, mocking how youthful and unqualified some executives seem.
summary: A toddler in a diaper turns out to be the company's new technology chief, dispensing sophisticated jargon until his bodily needs interrupt the meeting.

file: 2000/2000-09-06_single cell organism_new hire_break room_pretending.gif
title: New Hire Is A Blob

transcript.speaker: Bald Manager
transcript.text: So, I hear you're a single-cell organism.

transcript.speaker: Bald Manager
transcript.text: What's up with that?

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: The new guy is rolling into a ball and shedding water.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Been there.

situation: A bald, bespectacled manager interviews a new hire who looks like a shapeless blob sitting in a chair, asking about being a single-cell organism. The blob does not respond, and Alice reports that the new guy is rolling into a ball and shedding water. Dilbert replies that he has been there.
punchline: Dilbert's dry 'Been there' implies that curling up and shedding water under the stress of a job interview or the workplace is something he knows firsthand.
summary: A manager grills an amoeba-like job candidate while a coworker's remark about his defensive behavior draws a weary, relatable response from Dilbert.

file: 2000/2000-07-20_company identified_deadly falling satelites_investigative reporter_plan worked_falling satellites_hit target_boss thought plnned.gif
title: Satellite Crushes Boss's Living Room

transcript.speaker: TV Reporter
transcript.text: Our investigative reporter has identified the company behind the deadly falling satellites.

transcript.speaker: Sound Effect
transcript.text: WHUMP!

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Your plan worked.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: What plan?

setting: The Boss's living room at home, then the office
situation: A man in a recliner watches a TV news report about the company responsible for deadly falling satellites. A loud thump follows, implying a satellite has hit the TV or the room. In the last panel the boss thanks Dilbert for a plan that worked, and Dilbert has no idea what he is talking about.
punchline: The boss assumes Dilbert deliberately orchestrated an elaborate scheme, when Dilbert knows nothing about any plan, implying the satellite strike was a coincidence or the boss's own misplaced belief in a plot.
summary: A news report on killer satellites is cut short by a crash, and afterward a baffled Dilbert is credited with a scheme he never made.

file: 2000/2000-01-17_ceo_financial sunsidary_million victims_first year_cross selling_bayonet the survivors.gif
title: Dogbert's Predatory Financial Subsidiary Plan

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Mister Dogbert will be CEO of our financial subsidiary.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: My goal is one million victims in the first year.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: Then I'll do some cross-selling, which I prefer to call "bayonetting the survivors."

situation: At a meeting, the Boss announces that Dogbert will run the company's new financial subsidiary. Dogbert, seated at the table, openly states his goal is a million victims in the first year. He then describes cross-selling to those same customers as 'bayonetting the survivors' while Dilbert and the Boss look on.
punchline: Dogbert frankly admits that his financial business model is to prey on customers and then exploit the ones who remain, exposing how predatory cross-selling really is.
summary: A newly appointed canine executive cheerfully lays out a plan to fleece customers and then sell more to whoever is left.

file: 2000/2000-02-14_drive carefully_drive into a tree_policy_using cell phones_poisonous snakes_sarcasm_joking_obvious.gif
title: Cell Phone Policy Mocks Obvious Rules

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: The new policy says you must drive carefully while using cell phones.

transcript.speaker: Employee
transcript.text: This policy is just in time. I had planned to drive into a tree.

transcript.speaker: Employee
transcript.text: Is there anything there about handling poisonous snakes?

setting: Conference room table during a meeting
situation: The Boss reads aloud a new company policy requiring employees to drive carefully while using cell phones. A coworker sarcastically says the policy came just in time because he planned to drive into a tree. He then asks whether the policy also covers handling poisonous snakes.
punchline: The employee sarcastically mocks the policy for stating the obvious, implying it treats staff as people who need to be told not to do absurdly dangerous things.
summary: A coworker answers a patronizingly obvious safety policy with deadpan jokes about suicidal driving and venomous reptiles.

file: 2000/2000-09-08_uninterrupted_productivity_crumbs in sink_black sheep.gif
title: Posse Hunts Crumbs in Sink

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Today I will know the joy of uninterrupted productivity.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: We're forming a posse to find out who leaves crumbs in the sink.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I assume it's you.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: We need more black sheep around here.

situation: Dilbert sits at his computer hoping for a day of uninterrupted work. The Boss shows up holding a coffee mug and announces he's forming a posse to find whoever leaves crumbs in the sink. Dilbert assumes the culprit is the Boss himself, and the Boss responds that the company needs more black sheep.
punchline: The Boss, who is clearly the one leaving crumbs, cheerfully takes the accusation as a compliment, and his trivial posse interrupts Dilbert's hoped-for productive day.
summary: A man craving a quiet, productive day gets interrupted by his boss's petty kitchen-cleanliness crusade and then accuses the boss of being the real offender.

file: 2000/2000-02-29_action items_filberts mother_gnp_not giving back_tuition money_costs for strategy.gif
title: Wasted Effort Boosts GNP, Not Refunds

transcript.speaker: Dilbert's Mom
transcript.text: Did you do any action items this week?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I gathered costs for a strategy we had already decided not to use.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert's Mom
transcript.text: That helps the ol' GNP.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I'm not giving back your tuition money.

setting: Living room at his mother's home
situation: Dilbert's mother asks him over a cup of tea whether he completed any action items at work this week. He admits his only task was pricing out a strategy the team had already decided not to pursue. She cheerfully says that helps the economy, and he replies that he still won't return her tuition money.
punchline: Dilbert's mother treats even pointless make-work as economic activity that benefits GNP, while Dilbert wryly concedes that the useless job doesn't justify his expensive education.
summary: A son admits to his mom that his week's work was futile busywork, and she spins it as good for the economy.

file: 2000/2000-04-25_social misfits_keep him away_normal people_engineering liason.gif
title: Engineering Liaison: Guarding Normal People

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Dilbert is one of our social misfits.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Your job is to keep him away from normal people.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Hello! I'm right here!

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Your title will be "Engineering Liaison."

situation: The Boss introduces a new co-worker to Dilbert and describes him as a social misfit while Dilbert sits at his computer. He tells her that her job is to keep Dilbert away from normal people. Dilbert objects that he is right there, and the Boss continues, assigning her the title "Engineering Liaison."
punchline: The Boss insults Dilbert to his face as if he were not present, then dresses up the babysitting job with a grand-sounding title.
summary: A manager talks about an engineer as if he were invisible, handing a colleague the job of keeping him away from others under a fancy title.
keywords: talking about someone in front of them

file: 2000/2000-07-08_alice screams_jaw unhinges_mad_frighten hoagie_lunch room_break room_screams at lulu_frightening.gif
title: Alice Unhinges Jaw Demanding Input

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Lulu, you've stalled my project for long enough. I want your input...

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: NOW!!

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: I found out my jaw unhinges when I'm mad.

transcript.speaker: Coworker
transcript.text: You frighten my hoagie.

setting: Office cubicle area and break room
situation: Alice confronts a coworker named Lulu, who has been stalling her project, and demands her input. When Lulu doesn't respond, Alice screams at her with her jaw stretched impossibly wide. Later in the break room, Alice calmly explains her discovery to coworkers who are eating lunch, and one of them says she frightens his sandwich.
punchline: Alice's rage is so intense that her jaw literally unhinges, and a coworker's deadpan reaction is that she scares his hoagie rather than himself.
summary: A furious Alice screams at a project-stalling colleague with a dislocated jaw, then casually mentions the new talent over lunch.

file: 2000/2000-02-20_division_unusually profictable_targets impossibly high_profit target_sabotage profits_stop customers_wasteful spending_leadership training_class_stick out coffee mug.gif
title: Sabotaging Profits to Dodge Targets

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Our division is unusually profitable this year.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: That means our targets for next year will be set impossibly high.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Our only hope of reaching our profit target next year...

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: ...is to sabotage profits for the rest of this year.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: It's too late to stop customers from buying our products.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: So we'll focus on increasing our wasteful spending.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Wally, I'm sending you to a leadership training class.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: Did you ever stick out your coffee mug and just follow where it took you?

setting: Conference room during a management meeting
situation: At a meeting, the division's management realizes that an unusually profitable year will lead to impossibly high targets next year. The Boss proposes deliberately sabotaging this year's profits, and the group decides to boost wasteful spending since they can't stop customers from buying. The Boss then announces he's sending Wally to leadership training, and Wally responds with an absurd coffee-mug navigation anecdote.
punchline: The company punishes success with ever-higher targets, so managers deliberately waste money, and the leadership training turns out to be as nonsensical as the strategy it supports.
summary: Managers fearing the burden of future targets plot to squander this year's earnings, then send a coworker off to a leadership class that teaches silliness.

file: 2000/2000-04-17_huge severance package_last four emplyees_get fired_can retire.gif
title: One More Firing Until Retirement

transcript.speaker: Ken
transcript.text: I got huge severance packages from my last four employers.

transcript.speaker: Ken
transcript.text: If I get fired one more time I can retire.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Ken, we need to talk.

transcript.speaker: Sound effect
transcript.text: Ka-ching!

setting: Office break area where coworkers chat over coffee
situation: Ken brags to Dilbert and a bald coworker that he has collected big severance packages from his last four employers and could retire if fired once more. As he finishes, the boss walks up and tells him they need to talk. Ken's gesture and the 'ka-ching' sound suggest he sees another payout coming.
punchline: Ken's wish to be fired for one more severance check seems to come true the moment the boss asks to talk, and he treats it as a cash register ringing.
summary: A man who has profited from repeated layoffs gets summoned by his boss right as he muses about one more payout.

file: 2000/2000-08-06_video cameras installed_id badges_internet_phone use monitored_drug testing_hot irons_brand awareness_branding_employees_business_technology.gif
title: Catbert Brands Employees With Hot Irons

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Catbert: Evil H.R. Director

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: Video cameras have been installed in all work areas.

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: Employees must wear I.D. badges around their necks.

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: Your Internet and telephone usage will be monitored.

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: Everyone will undergo mandatory drug testing.

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: They're not resisting. They're ready for phase two.

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: Prepare to be permanently marked by hot irons.

transcript.speaker: Employee
transcript.text: Will that hurt?

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: I'll be fine. Thanks for asking.

transcript.speaker: Catbert
transcript.text: Wally is about to experience brand awareness.

setting: Conference room during an HR announcement
situation: Catbert, the evil HR director, announces escalating workplace policies to a meeting of employees: cameras, ID badges, monitoring, and drug testing. When the staff meekly accept everything, he concludes they are ready for phase two and announces they will be branded with hot irons. In the last panel Wally is held down and branded.
punchline: After employees passively accept ever more invasive controls, Catbert literally brands them, turning the corporate phrase 'brand awareness' into a painful pun, while his reply to 'Will that hurt?' shows he only cares about himself.
summary: An HR villain tests how much surveillance workers will swallow, then moves on to literally branding them with red-hot irons.

file: 2000/2000-06-09_two faced_employee_see one_turn around_other faces_confusing_frustrating_pointing.gif
title: Where's The Other Face?

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: I disagree with Dilbert. The Boss's plan is brilliant.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Your other face agreed with me two minutes ago!

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: What other face?

transcript.speaker: Boss
transcript.text: No... I still just see the one.

situation: At a meeting, Wally publicly praises the Boss's plan and says he disagrees with Dilbert. Dilbert accuses Wally of being two-faced, since he agreed with Dilbert just minutes ago, but Wally plays dumb and asks what other face. Dilbert gestures at Wally in frustration while the Boss literally looks for a second face and finds only one.
punchline: The Boss takes the 'two-faced' accusation literally, so Wally's flattery goes unchallenged and Dilbert's valid complaint about his hypocrisy is dismissed.
summary: A coworker who flip-flops to flatter the boss is called out for having two faces, and the clueless boss takes the insult as a literal statement and fails to see the point.

file: 2000/2000-08-25_sitting in a box_checking stocks_cucbicle_job_stock market_this is life_computer_money_survival_business_technology.gif
title: Dilbert Obsessively Checking His Stocks

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I'm sittin' in a box and checkin' my stocks.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I must use all my willpower to resist checking every ten seconds.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I'm sittin' in a box and checkin' my stocks.

situation: Dilbert sits alone at his computer in his cubicle, thinking in thought bubbles. He describes his day as sitting in a box checking his stocks, then claims he is straining to resist checking them every ten seconds. In the last panel he repeats his first thought, showing he has been checking all along.
punchline: Dilbert claims to be resisting the urge to check his stocks every ten seconds, but his repeated thought shows he is checking them constantly anyway.
summary: A cubicle worker boasts of heroic self-restraint over his portfolio while his looping thoughts reveal he cannot stop watching it.

file: 2000/2000-08-27_replaced computers_training class_ignored requests_sit unused_slow way_computer manual_no time_class_coat_invest_plan future.gif
title: No Time to Read the Manual

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: So they replaced our computers and never trained us.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I told them we needed a training class but they ignored my requests.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: So our computers sit there unused while we do our work the slow way.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Why don't you read the computer manual?

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I don't have time for that!

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: But you have time for a class? It doesn't add up.

transcript.speaker: Woman
transcript.text: I'm cold.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: You should try wearing a coat. They're terrific.

setting: Outdoors on a hiking trail in the hills
situation: A coworker complains to Dilbert while they walk that her department got new computers but no training, so the machines sit unused while staff work the slow way. Dilbert suggests reading the manual, and she says she has no time, yet she wanted time for a class. When she then says she's cold, Dilbert sarcastically suggests wearing a coat.
punchline: Dilbert mocks her by answering her complaint about being cold with the same kind of obvious fix she keeps rejecting for the computers, a cheap simple solution she refuses to take.
summary: A woman grumbles about untrained use of new equipment, rejects the easy fix of reading instructions, and then gets the same sort of blunt advice when she complains of the chill.

file: 2000/2000-06-08_boss_edfred_freak_new hire_new plan_trust_two faced employee_two headed.gif
title: Two-Faced Employee Sets Trap

transcript.speaker: Edfred
transcript.text: Hi, I'm Edfred, the two-faced employee.

transcript.speaker: Edfred
transcript.text: If you tell your boss his new plan is stupid I'll back you up.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Really?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I don't like the looks of this.

setting: Office cubicle, then a conference room
situation: A new coworker introduces himself to Dilbert as 'the two-faced employee' and then offers to back him up if he tells the boss his new plan is stupid. Dilbert is skeptical, and in the meeting room he sits across from Edfred, who smirks while the boss sits at the table, and Dilbert suspects a setup.
punchline: Edfred openly announces that he is two-faced, so his offer of support is obviously a trap, and Dilbert is right to distrust him.
summary: A self-declared backstabber promises to support Dilbert in criticizing the boss, which Dilbert rightly smells as a setup.

file: 2000/2000-03-14_irs in jail_swelled up_basket case_women hate summaries_beach ball_head swelled.gif
title: Dilbert Summarizes His Date Badly

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: ...So my head swelled up like a beach ball and the I.R.S. wants to put me in jail.

transcript.speaker: Date
transcript.text: In summary, you're a basket case.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Women hate it when you summarize.

setting: A restaurant table during a date, then Dilbert's living room at home
situation: Dilbert is on a dinner date and rambles about his head swelling like a beach ball and the IRS wanting to jail him. His date sums him up bluntly as a basket case. Afterward, home alone with Dogbert, Dilbert complains that women hate being summarized.
punchline: Dilbert blames the date's failure on her summarizing, when her accurate summary was the honest verdict on his disastrous, self-inflicted mess.
summary: After a dinner date goes badly, a man blames his companion's blunt wrap-up rather than the alarming story he told her.

file: 2000/2000-01-09_added up columns_grocery list_marketing starategy_pros and cons_quantified_unhealthy.gif
title: Pros and Cons Grocery List

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I quantified our marketing strategy because you insisted.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I listed the pros and cons on this sheet.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Then I added up the columns.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: The pros outnumber the cons, so we're going forward.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Let's see. Your cons include... unhealthy and unprofitable.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Your pros are.. waffles, eggs, bananas and milk.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Oops. That might be my grocery list.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: You fool! I told you quantification never works!!

situation: Dilbert reports that he quantified the marketing strategy by listing pros and cons and counting them, concluding the project should proceed. The Boss reads the sheet and discovers the pros are waffles, eggs, bananas and milk, and Dilbert admits it may be his grocery list. The Boss then shouts that this proves quantification never works.
punchline: The Boss blames the method for the failure instead of recognizing that Dilbert handed him a grocery list, using the mistake as vindication of his own distrust of data.
summary: A mix-up between a marketing analysis and a shopping list lets a manager claim that measuring things is pointless.

file: 2000/2000-04-03_fake disability claim_disabled_hard to believe_note from doctor_obvious_long time.gif
title: Wally's Fake Disability Claim

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: I'm thinking about going out on a fake disability claim.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: Do you think anyone will believe I'm disabled?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: It's hard to believe you're not.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: Do you need a note from my doctor?

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: No, it's been obvious for a long time.

setting: Office coffee station, then the boss's office
situation: Wally tells Dilbert at the coffee machine that he is considering a fake disability claim and asks whether anyone would believe it. Dilbert replies that it's hard to believe he isn't disabled. Wally then asks his boss if he needs a doctor's note, and the boss says it has been obvious for a long time.
punchline: Everyone assumes Wally is already disabled because of his incompetence and laziness, so his fake claim is automatically credible and he needs no proof.
summary: A slacker plans to fake a disability and discovers his colleagues and manager already think there is something wrong with him.

file: 2000/2000-01-29_stressed out_work_feel better_verbally abused_co worker_money spit_use that one.gif
title: Stress Relief Through Insulting Coworkers

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I'm stressed out about work. Maybe I'd feel better if I verbally abused a co-worker.

transcript.speaker: Co-worker
transcript.text: You worthless piece of monkey spit!

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Dang. I was going to use that one.

transcript.speaker: Co-worker
transcript.text: Aah...

situation: Dilbert, sitting in a meeting, thinks to himself that he might feel better if he verbally abused a co-worker. Before he can act, a nearby co-worker suddenly shouts an insult, using the very line Dilbert had in mind. The co-worker leans back, relieved, while Dilbert grumbles that his insult was taken.
punchline: Dilbert is annoyed not by being insulted but by a co-worker beating him to the stress-relieving insult he planned to use, while the co-worker enjoys the catharsis.
summary: A worker pondering insulting a colleague to relieve stress gets scooped when someone else in the meeting vents with the exact insult he had in mind.

file: 2000/2000-01-27_back in 10_managers_over  communicate_times of uncertainty_you're fired_ted fired.gif
title: Over-Communicating Fired Over and Over

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Ed, the experts say managers should over-communicate during times of uncertainty.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: You're fired, you're fired, you're fired, you're fired, you're fired!

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I'll come back in ten minutes to do that again.

situation: The Boss tells an employee named Ed that experts advise managers to over-communicate during uncertain times. He then shouts "You're fired" repeatedly at the stunned employee. He announces he'll return in ten minutes to repeat the process.
punchline: The Boss takes the advice to over-communicate literally and applies it to the worst possible message, repeatedly firing the same employee and promising to do it again.
summary: A manager misapplies a communication tip by repeatedly announcing a termination to a bewildered subordinate and planning an encore.

file: 2000/2000-02-04_waiting_stock isn't vested_over flow_limbo_hell.gif
title: Stuck at Work: Overflow From Limbo

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I can't do anything because I'm always waiting for someone else.

transcript.speaker: Devil
transcript.text: And you can't quit because your stock isn't vested.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Am I in heck?

transcript.speaker: Devil
transcript.text: No, I'm just working the overflow from limbo.

situation: Dilbert sits at his computer thinking about how he can't get anything done because he is always waiting on other people. A devil in a red hooded costume carrying a large spoon appears and points out he can't quit either, because his stock options aren't vested. Dilbert asks whether he is in hell, and the devil says no, he is just handling the overflow from limbo.
punchline: Dilbert's workplace is so stuck and inescapable that it is not even hell, just the overflow area for limbo, a place of endless waiting.
summary: A devil informs a trapped, stalled employee that his job is merely the spillover from limbo rather than actual hell.

file: 2000/2000-06-11_cut budget_technology installation_adequate budget_unethical vendors_huge purchase_free stuff_no hidden costs_huge purchase later.gif
title: Boss Teaches Vendor Deception for Free Stuff

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I cut your budget in half.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: How can I do a technology installation without an adequate budget?!

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Try being unethical with our vendors.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: It's easy.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Tell them we might make a huge purchase later...

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: ...if they give us a bunch of free stuff now.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: If it makes you feel better, wait until THEY lie first.

transcript.speaker: Vendor
transcript.text: And there are no hidden costs.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Um...we might make a huge purchase later.

setting: The Boss's office, then a vendor's office
situation: The Boss halves Dilbert's budget for a technology installation, then advises him to be unethical with vendors by promising a big future purchase in exchange for free goods now. He even suggests waiting for the vendors to lie first. In the final panel, Dilbert meets a vendor who claims there are no hidden costs, and Dilbert dutifully repeats the Boss's empty promise.
punchline: Both buyer and seller are lying through their teeth, and the Boss's cost-cutting plan amounts to institutionalized dishonesty that Dilbert ends up carrying out.
summary: After slashing a budget, the Boss coaches his engineer to bluff suppliers with fake promises of future business, and the engineer ends up doing exactly that.

file: 2000/2000-07-02_system failures_data aren't actionable_no practical value_crime_guilty_feel awkward_incident.gif
title: Fifteen Failures, Zero Actionable Data

transcript.speaker: Presenter
transcript.text: We had fifteen system failures with the previous software.

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Your data aren't actionable.

transcript.speaker: Presenter
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: Your presentation has no practical value.

transcript.speaker: Presenter
transcript.text: Well, if that's suddenly a crime then call me guilty!

transcript.speaker: Dilbert
transcript.text: I guess.

transcript.speaker: Bald Coworker
transcript.text: Now the meeting feels awkward. Can we go back to acting interested?

transcript.speaker: Presenter
transcript.text: Fine. Let's put this ugly incident behind us.

transcript.speaker: Presenter
transcript.text: And if you multiply the digits you get five.

situation: A presenter shows a single slide reporting fifteen system failures with the previous software. Dilbert and a bald coworker bluntly criticize the data as not actionable and without practical value. After a tense exchange and a pretense of restoring politeness, the presenter resumes with a pointless extra fact about the number.
punchline: Having just been told his data is useless, the presenter proceeds to offer an even more meaningless observation about the number fifteen, showing he learned nothing from the criticism.
summary: A presenter's single-number slide gets rejected as useless, and after a brief truce he follows up with an equally pointless numerical trivia fact.

file: 2000/2000-01-20_dogcart investments_1% annual fee_invest money_certified financial planner_make money.gif
title: Dogbert Charges Fee for Middleman

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: For a 1% annual fee I will invest your money with a certified financial planner.

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: He'll charge 1% per year to put your money in mutual funds that charge 1% per year.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Will I make any money?

transcript.speaker: Dogbert
transcript.text: I don't see you doing any of the work.

situation: Dogbert, running Dogbert Investments, offers the Boss a service where he passes the Boss's money to a certified financial planner for a 1% annual fee. He explains that the planner charges another 1% to put the money into mutual funds that charge yet another 1%. When the Boss asks whether he will actually make money, Dogbert replies that the Boss isn't doing any of the work.
punchline: Layers of middlemen each take a 1% cut, so the investor pays everyone and earns nothing, and Dogbert dismisses the Boss's return as unearned since he does no work.
summary: A cynical dog financial adviser reveals that every link in an investment chain skims a fee, leaving the client's profit as an afterthought.

file: 2000/2000-04-01_gap analysis_honest_two pointy hairs_for department.gif
title: Gap Analysis Between Pointy Hairs

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: I want you to perform a gap analysis for our department.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Be completely honest.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: The gap is located between two pointy tufts of hair that move about the office.

setting: Office, the boss's desk and Dilbert's cubicle
situation: The Boss, seated at his desk, asks Dilbert to perform a gap analysis for the department and to be completely honest. Dilbert then types at his computer, and the on-screen text reveals that the 'gap' is the space between the Boss's two pointy tufts of hair.
punchline: Dilbert uses a literal reading of 'gap' and the Boss's own invitation to be honest to call the Boss himself the department's gap, meaning the Boss is the problem.
summary: Told to candidly analyze what is lacking in his department, an employee pins the blame squarely on his boss's head.

file: 2000/2000-07-26_three days_repair guy_under desk_uninvited_feeds licorice_animals_feed animals_i.s. people.gif
title: Feeding the I.S. Guy Licorice

transcript.speaker: Bald coworker
transcript.text: How long has he been under your desk?

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Three days.

transcript.speaker: Bald coworker
transcript.text: Did you feed him?

transcript.speaker: Alice
transcript.text: Just some licorice.

transcript.speaker: Bald coworker
transcript.text: You should never feed the I.S. people.

transcript.speaker: I.S. person (under desk)
transcript.text: More licorice!

situation: A bald coworker with a coffee mug asks Alice how long an I.S. technician has been under her desk, and she says three days. She admits she has only fed him licorice, and he warns her never to feed the I.S. people. A hand reaches out from under the desk demanding more licorice.
punchline: Treating the I.S. technicians like stray animals that become dependent once fed, the strip shows one now refusing to leave and demanding more treats.
summary: A technician has camped under a cubicle for days, and a well-meaning snack has turned him into a demanding pest.

file: 2000/2000-02-22_technology_paul tergeist_computer_shoots up_falls on head_dilbert_coworker_monitor head.gif
title: Paul Tergeist and the Flying Monitor

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: This technology will work or my name isn't Paul Tergeist.

transcript.speaker: Wally
transcript.text: I wish I had a nickel for every time that happened to a co-worker.

transcript.speaker: Co-worker
transcript.text: Ow.

situation: A bald, tie-wearing co-worker tells Dilbert, who is typing at his computer, that the technology will work or his name isn't Paul Tergeist. A computer monitor then flies up and out of frame, on a cord, and comes crashing down onto the head of the person typing, leaving him wearing it like a helmet. The first co-worker remarks that he'd be rich if he got a nickel every time that happened to a co-worker.
punchline: The man's guarantee that the technology will work is instantly disproven by the monitor launching itself onto the typist's head, and his casual remark implies such computer mishaps happen so routinely in this office that they're an everyday occurrence.
summary: A confident promise that new equipment will work is promptly undone when a monitor launches itself onto an unlucky colleague's head, prompting a deadpan remark about how common such accidents are.

file: 2000/2000-05-25_ceo spokeperson_pose_prodcut_blue screen technology_important elements_blue blouse.gif
title: Blue Screen Blouse Problem

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: CEO as spokesperson

transcript.speaker: CEO
transcript.text: What does this pose have to do with our product?

transcript.speaker: Photographer
transcript.text: I'll use blue screen technology to add important elements later.

transcript.speaker: CEO
transcript.text: My blouse is blue.

transcript.speaker: Photographer
transcript.text: Five minutes.

situation: A female CEO is posed bent over a chair for a promotional photo shoot and asks what the pose has to do with the product. The photographer, a white creature in a red beret, says he will use blue screen technology to add the important elements later. When the CEO points out that her blouse is blue, he immediately tells her she has five minutes, implying she should change into something else.
punchline: The photographer's real interest is in getting the CEO to remove or change her blue top, exposing that the suggestive pose and the blue screen excuse are a pretext for ogling her rather than promoting a product.
summary: A photographer uses a technical excuse to nudge a posing executive toward showing more than her marketing campaign requires.

file: 2000/2000-06-03_turn invisible_run silent_make descions_can't see.gif
title: Boss Wishes He Were Invisible

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: If I could turn invisible, I wouldn't need to make decisions.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Invisible... invisible... you can't see me.

transcript.speaker: Carol
transcript.text: I guess we're done.

transcript.speaker: The Boss
transcript.text: Run silent.

situation: Carol stands at the Boss's desk waiting for him to make a decision. The Boss daydreams about turning invisible so he would never have to decide anything, then tries to will himself invisible while Carol watches. Carol gives up and says they're done, while the Boss keeps hiding in his thoughts.
punchline: The Boss would rather try to vanish than make a decision, and he succeeds only in avoiding the decision because Carol gives up on him.
summary: A boss tries to dodge a decision by wishing himself invisible, and his assistant finally walks away from the standoff.
